title: Generative AI at Work: Core Argument Coverage Plan
subtitle: Impact of LLM-based Assistants on Customer Support Productivity and Organization

nodes.title: Research Question & Context
nodes.purpose: Define the study's objective: measuring the economic impact of generative AI in a real-world workplace, specifically focusing on productivity, skill bias, and organizational outcomes.

nodes.title: AI System Mechanism & Tacit Knowledge
nodes.purpose: Explain how the tool works (LLM fine-tuned on chat history) and the core hypothesis: it captures and disseminates 'tacit knowledge' from high-skill workers to low-skill workers.

nodes.title: Empirical Strategy & Identification
nodes.purpose: Detail the staggered deployment design, Difference-in-Differences model (Eq. 1), and handling of heterogeneous treatment effects using Sun & Abraham (2021) estimator.

nodes.title: Main Result: Productivity Increase
nodes.purpose: Present the primary finding: 14% average increase in resolutions per hour, driven by reduced handle time and increased multitasking capacity.

nodes.title: Heterogeneity: Skill-Biased Change
nodes.purpose: Analyze the distributional impact: largest gains for novice/low-skill workers (35% increase) vs. minimal/no gain for experts, contrasting with prior IT literature.

nodes.title: Mechanism Evidence: Experience Curve Acceleration
nodes.purpose: Show evidence that AI helps new agents reach the productivity level of experienced agents much faster (2 months vs. 6+ months).

nodes.title: Textual Evidence: Convergence in Communication
nodes.purpose: Present textual analysis showing low-skill agents' language becomes more similar to high-skill agents post-AI, supporting the tacit knowledge transfer hypothesis.

nodes.title: Organizational Outcomes: Sentiment & Retention
nodes.purpose: Report secondary findings: improved customer sentiment, reduced escalation requests, and lower employee attrition, particularly for newer workers.

nodes.title: Adherence & Implementation Dynamics
nodes.purpose: Discuss the correlation between following AI recommendations and productivity gains, and how adherence evolves over time across skill groups.

nodes.title: Limitations & Scope Conditions
nodes.purpose: Clarify boundaries: results apply to stable product environments, do not address aggregate wage/employment effects, and highlight compensation questions for data providers.

coverage_notes: The argument flows from the theoretical mechanism (tacit knowledge capture) to empirical identification (staggered DiD), then to heterogeneous results (skill bias), and finally to mechanistic evidence (textual similarity) and broader organizational impacts.
Core formulas include the DiD specification (Eq. 1, p.12) and the definition of key variables like Resolutions Per Hour (p.11).
Visual evidence from Figures 3-15 supports the quantitative claims regarding distributions, event studies, and heterogeneity.
